name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based motion capture datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL body model parameters. AMASS contains more than 40 hours of motion data, 346 subjects, and 11451 motions, and provides SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue motion parameters, including articulated hands when markers are present.
creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Gerard Pons-Moll; Nikolaus F. Troje; Michael J. Black
citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Gerard Pons-Moll, Nikolaus F. Troje, Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1, 2019.
rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by unifying 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common SMPL parameterization using MoSh++. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, while several others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors themselves, including Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM. The source datasets were recorded using different numbers of markers placed at different body locations, and even within a dataset the number of markers varies. For the SSM dataset used to tune and evaluate MoSh++, the authors used an OptiTrack motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system to capture subjects wearing 67 reflective markers.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. The method introduces a coefficient based on the number of missing markers in a frame to increase the pose prior weight when markers are missing.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are archival optical marker-based human motion capture datasets and, for SSM, synchronized marker-based mocap and 4D body scans. AMASS uses marker data from 15 datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors used MoSh++ to map marker data from the source datasets into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. They manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems caused by inherent mocap issues such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To create AMASS, the source mocap datasets with varying marker sets were converted into a unified SMPL representation using MoSh++. For SSM hyperparameter tuning, the authors separated sequences into training and testing sets, used 12 randomly chosen frames from subject-specific sequences for shape estimation, and used held-out motion files and frame subsets for pose estimation validation. In fitting, the method scales the data term according to the number of observed markers and adjusts the pose prior according to the number of missing markers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset does not describe human semantic labeling of examples; instead, MoSh++ fits SMPL/SMPL-H+DMPL body model parameters to observed mocap markers. Each frame in AMASS includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations. The authors also manually inspected results and corrected or held out problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For SSM, hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation and scan-to-model distances between synchronized 3D scans and estimated meshes. The authors report average scan-to-mesh distances and use held-out validation and test sets. They also note that adding more shape or dynamic coefficients can overfit to markers, increasing error relative to ground-truth shape.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++; SMPL; SMPL-H; DMPL; MANO; Chumpy
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state that with MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and they will continue to expand the dataset. They will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared, and conclude that they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by the authors and the community.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape; hand articulation; motion data; 3D body scans of subjects. The dataset includes over 300 subjects with varying body shapes.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the consistent representation of AMASS makes it useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning, and that it enables new applications that require large amounts of training data.
rai:dataBiases: The source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The paper also notes that datasets vary in format, kinematic structure, and marker sets, and that allowing more shape variation with limited markers can result in overfitting.
rai:dataLimitations: Existing source mocap datasets are described as often narrowly focused on particular motion classes. AMASS inherits inherent mocap problems such as swapped, mislabeled, and occluded markers, requiring manual inspection and correction or exclusion. Hand articulation is only estimated when hand markers are present; otherwise hand poses are set to the average MANO pose. The current runtime of MoSh++ is not real-time. The SSM evaluation dataset contains only three subjects, and the paper notes that they do not have ground-truth data for evaluating hand articulation accuracy.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for research use in animation, visualization, generating training data for deep learning, computer vision, and learning models of human motion. The paper states that AMASS enables applications that require large amounts of training data and can be leveraged to train models that denoise mocap data.
